Leah Stewart was bitten by a shark at Sydney's Coogee Beach during a morning swim

An Australian woman bitten by a shark at a popular Sydney beach earlier this year says she has been given a "second chance at life" and will be making the most of it.

Leah Stewart, 35, was mauled by a shark during a morning swim at Coogee Beach in June, suffering multiple bites to her arms and legs, amid a spate of attacks in Australia.

The mother-of-one was placed in an induced coma and had several surgeries, including having one of her arms amputated.

In an online post on Monday, she thanked her supporters who have raised more than AU$550,000 (US$394,000; £289,000) for her, saying her recovery has been "incredibly difficult" but she is making "remarkable" progress.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," Stewart wrote, in her first comments since the attack.

"I want you to know that I feel like I've been given a second chance at life, and I'm not going to waste it."

Stewart said she had been "overwhelmed" by the support from family, friends and "even strangers", adding that the "you've inspired me to get better, not bitter".

An online fundraiser for her would now be closed, she wrote, with the money raised giving her the chance to recover at home as well as "options for further medical treatment down the road".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable, and a huge part of that is because of the absolute army of love, support, prayers and encouragement surrounding my family and I from all over the world."

There have been a spate of shark attacks in Australia this year, with four attacks over a two-day period in January, including one on a 12-year-old boy who later died from his injuries.

In May, a man was killed by a shark in Queensland while spearfishing and in Western Australia, a father-of-two died after he was attacked by a 4m (13ft) shark.

Shark attack victim Leah Stewart has spoken for the first time about her recovery more than two months after she was mauled by a white shark at Coogee Beach.

On a fundraising site, she wrote that her recovery was ongoing, but that she had been given a second chance at life and was not going to waste it.

She also thanked the community for its generosity after more than $500,000 was raised.

Sydney shark attack victim Leah Stewart says she has not fully recovered more than two months after the incident, but feels like she has been given a "second chance at life".

Ms Stewart's family had previously provided updates on her condition on a fundraising site. Yesterday, she wrote for the first time about her experience.

"After what has been an incredibly difficult few months, I'm so happy that I've progressed enough to build some independence, and I can finally see some light after all of this," she said.

Leah Stewart says the past few months have been "incredibly difficult". (Supplied: Stewart family)

On June 13, Ms Stewart was taken to St Vincent's Hospital in a critical condition after being mauled by a white shark while she was out for a morning swim, between the flags and close to the shore, at Coogee Beach in Sydney's east.

The 35-year-old was bitten on her leg and arms, suffered multiple fractures throughout her body and lost a lot of blood.

She was in an induced coma for days and underwent multiple surgeries, including the amputation of one of her arms.

The mother of one said she has been focusing on her healing and doing everything in her "power to get back to some sort of normal life".

"I still have a long way to go, but my recovery has been remarkable."

More than $500,000 has been raised to aid her recuperation, and while Ms Stewart profusely thanked the community for its generosity, she said it was time to "turn off donations".

"Because what you've offered has given us enough to recover, to stay in our home, and to give us options for further medical treatment down the road," she said.

Leah Stewart says the support she has received has "inspired me to get better, not bitter". (Supplied: Stewart family)

She added the support she received locally and from around the world had contributed to her recovery.
